'''La Shawn K. Ford''' (born February 28, 1972)<ref>{{cite web | title=La Shawn K. Ford &#124; Chicago News &#124; WTTW | url=https://news.wttw.com/elections/voters-guide/2019/candidates/chicago-mayor/la-shawn-k-ford }}</ref> is an American politician who is a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] member of the [[Illinois House of Representatives]], representing the [[Illinois's 8th House of Representatives district|8th district]] since 2007. The district includes the West Side of Chicago and the suburbs of Oak Park, Berwyn, North Riverside, Forest Park, Proviso Township, Brookfield, La Grange Park, La Grange, and Western Springs.

Ford was a candidate for [[Mayor of Chicago]] in the [[2019 Chicago mayoral election|2019 election]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Preston|first=Charles|title=An Interview With Rep. LaShawn K. Ford: Will He Run For Mayor|newspaper=[[Chicago Defender]]|date=September 26, 2018|access-date=October 25, 2018|url=https://chicagodefender.com/2018/09/26/an-interview-with-rep-lashawn-k-ford-will-he-run-for-mayor/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928044427/https://chicagodefender.com/2018/09/26/an-interview-with-rep-lashawn-k-ford-will-he-run-for-mayor/|archive-date=September 28, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is the Democratic nominee for the [[United States House of Representatives]] in [[Illinois's 7th congressional district]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 7|2026 election]].<ref name="Congress">{{cite web|last=Mordacq|first=Jessica|url=https://www.austinweeklynews.com/2025/07/31/davis-endorsement/|title=Davis endorses La Shawn Ford, announces retirement|work=[[Austin Weekly News]]|date=July 31, 2025|accessdate=July 31, 2025}}</ref>

==Early life, education, and career==

Ford was born in Chicago's [[Cabrini–Green Homes|Cabrini–Green]] housing project.<ref name="wttwforum">{{cite web |last1=Blumberg |first1=Nick |title=Mayoral Candidate Forum: Chico, Enyia, Ford, Lightfoot, McCarthy |url=https://news.wttw.com/2019/02/19/mayoral-candidate-forum-chico-enyia-ford-lightfoot-mccarthy |publisher=WTTW News |access-date=28 December 2019 |language=en |date=19 February 2019}}</ref> He grew up in the [[Austin, Chicago|Austin]] community of Chicago.<ref name="wttwforum" /> His family moved to the Austin community when he was two years old.<ref name="lfcrusader" /> Ford never met his father.<ref name="lfcrusader" /> His mother was an unwed teen, and he was adopted by his grandmother at birth.<ref name="lfcrusader" />

Ford attended Lady Help of Christians Catholic Elementary School and graduated from [[Weber High School (Chicago)|Weber High School]].<ref name=lfcrusader/>

Initially, after high school, Ford attended the [[Niles College Seminary]] contemplating becoming a priest.<ref name=lfcrusader/> Ford ultimately received a bachelor of arts in elementary education with a minor in [[political science]] from [[Loyola University Chicago]].<ref name=lfcrusader/> He played basketball while at Loyola.<ref name=lfcrusader/> He also attended the [[University of Illinois, Chicago]].<ref name=lfcrusader/>

Ford became a history teacher and basketball coach for [[Chicago Public Schools]] at Bridge Elementary School on the northwest side. Later he became a licensed Illinois real estate broker, and became the founder of Ford Desired Real Estate in 2001.<ref name="First Reading 11/2006"/><ref name=lfcrusader/> He has served as a member of the Chicago and [[National Association of Realtors]], board member of the Austin YMCA, board member of Circle Family Care, board member of the Austin Chamber of Commerce, founding organizer of Zawadi Youth Group, and member of St. Martin de Porres Catholic Church Parish Council and Finance Committee.<ref name="ILGA Bio">{{cite web|title=Representative La Shawn K. Ford (D) 8th District|access-date=December 17, 2018|publisher=[[Illinois General Assembly]]|url=http://ilga.gov/house/rep.asp?MemberID=2356}}</ref>

Ford worked as a Democratic precinct captain in the neighborhood where he grew up.<ref name=lfcrusader/>

==Legislative career==
Ford was first elected to the Illinois House of Representatives in 2007, defeating incumbent [[Calvin Giles]] in the Democratic primary and winning the General Election with 83% of the vote.<ref name="First Reading 11/2006">
{{cite web|editor-last=Miller|editor-first=David R.|title=Biographies of New House Members|work=First Reading|publisher=Illinois Legislative Research Unit|date=November 15, 2006|volume=20|number=2|access-date=December 17, 2018|page=3|url=http://www.ilga.gov/commission/lru/nov2006firstrdg.pdf}}</ref>

Ford is focused on social justice and disparities in employment, education, and the healthcare system. He has worked to foster small business development, improve access to affordable housing, expand veterans' protections, safeguard the environment, and address Illinois' fiscal health. He also advocates for preserving communities, helping ex-offenders re-enter society, and enshrining the right to vote. He created a commission to confront economic problems that plague Black communities as well as the [https://www.ilga.gov/legislation/fulltext.asp?DocName=09800HR0095lv&SessionID=85&GA=98&DocTypeID=HR&DocNum=0095&SpecSess=&Session=&print=true Distressed Counties and Communities Task Force], which finds innovative ways to help people who receive state social services.

Throughout his career, Ford has chaired a number of committees: Appropriations—Higher Education; Financial Institutions, Restorative Justice. Ford's committee assignments are: the Appropriations Committee on Elementary & Secondary Education; Appropriations Committee on Human Services; Insurance: Property & Casualty; Tourism, Hospitality & Craft Industries; and Veterans' Affairs.<ref name="ILGA Bio" />

Ford is a member of the Medicaid Managed Care Oversight Task Force, which is intended to monitor how the State approaches and manages a new form of health care delivery system based on managed care models, particularly for people with disabilities and the elderly.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 31, 2018 |editor-last=Wolff |editor-first=Jonathan P. |title=47005 Medicaid Managed Care Oversight Task Force |url=http://www.ilga.gov/commission/lru/Gov.pdf |access-date=December 17, 2018 |work=Expiration and Vacancy Report for the Governor of Illinois |publisher=Illinois Legislative Research Unit |page=241}}</ref><ref name="Task Force List">{{cite web|last=Gruber|first=Amanda|title=Publication 425: State Board and Commission Descriptions|publisher=Illinois Legislative Research Unit|date=August 1, 2018|access-date=December 14, 2018|page=510|url=http://www.ilga.gov/commission/lru/Descriptions.pdf}}</ref> He is also a member of the Violence Prevention Task Force, which seeks to increase awareness of resources, jobs, and opportunities to prevent violence and to assist violence prevention groups and other social institutions in providing safe places for those at risk of violence.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 31, 2018 |editor-last=Wolff |editor-first=Jonathan P. |title=43033 Violence Prevention Task Force |url=http://www.ilga.gov/commission/lru/Gov.pdf |access-date=December 17, 2018 |work=Expiration and Vacancy Report for the Governor of Illinois |publisher=Illinois Legislative Research Unit |page=390}}</ref><ref name="Task Force List" />

From 2006 until 2012, Ford had received $16,350 in campaign contributions from [[Trade union|labor unions]]. This included $3,000 from [[AFL-CIO]], $2,650 from [[American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees|AFSCME]], $200 from [[National Education Association|Illinois Education Association]]; $2,500 from the [[American Federation of Teachers|Illinois Federation of Teachers]], $7,000 from the [[Chicago Teachers Union]], $1,000 from [[Service Employees International Union]].<ref>[http://www.followthemoney.org/database/uniquecandidate.phtml?uc=3404 "Candidate Summary - La Shawn K. Ford"], [[OpenSecrets]]</ref>

In 2020, Ford voiced support for the abolition of history classes in Illinois schools, claiming that "current history teaching practices overlook the contributions by Women and members of the Black, Jewish, LGBTQ communities and other groups" and "until a suitable alternative is developed, we should instead devote greater attention toward civics and ensuring students understand our democratic processes and how they can be involved".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chicago-Area Leaders Call for Illinois to Abolish History Classes|url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/chicago-area-leaders-call-for-illinois-to-eliminate-history-classes/2315752/|access-date=2021-01-27|website=NBC Chicago|date=3 August 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref>

As of July 2, 2022, Representative Ford is a member of the following Illinois House committees:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Illinois General Assembly - Representative Committees |url=https://ilga.gov/house/RepCommittees.asp?MemberID=2815 |access-date=2022-07-03 |website=ilga.gov}}</ref>

* (Chairman of) Appropriations - Higher Education Committee (HAPI)
* Fair Lending and Community Reinvestment Subcommittee (HFIN-FAIR)
* Financial Institutions Committee (HFIN)
* Labor & Commerce Committee (HLBR)
* Public Utilities Committee (HPUB)
* Restorative Justice Committee (SHRJ)

Ford also identifies himself as a firm believer in the power of responsible parenting and helped grow the [http://responsiblefatherhood.com/wp-content/uploads/2011/12/lashawnford-dailyherald.pdf Illinois Council on Responsible Fatherhood], which aims to support fathers and help them to become more responsible and present. He consistently advocates for increased access to financial resources and institutions for marginalized communities and promotes the value of education among students in his district.

==2019 mayoral campaign==
Ford ran for mayor of Chicago in 2019. After giving notice of a possible candidacy in late-September,<ref name=lfcrusader>{{cite web |title=La Shawn Ford enters race for mayor {{!}} The Crusader Newspaper Group |url=https://chicagocrusader.com/la-shawn-ford-enters-race-for-mayor/ |publisher=Chicago Crusader |access-date=28 December 2019 |date=27 September 2018}}</ref> Ford officially announced his candidacy on October 31, 2018, joining what was an already-crowded field of candidates seeking to replace [[Rahm Emanuel]], who had announced in early September that he would not seek reelection.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bremer |first1=Shelby |title=State Rep. La Shawn Ford Announces Run for Chicago Mayor |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/chicago-politics/lashawn-ford-running-for-chicago-mayor/169875/ |publisher=NBC Chicago |access-date=28 December 2019 |date=31 October 2018}}</ref>

Candidate [[Willie Wilson (businessman)|Willie Wilson]] challenged signatures on Ford's candidature petition, but the Chicago Board of Elections allowed Ford to remain on the ballot, finding that, "candidate Willie Wilson's objection to his petitions was not made in good faith."<ref>{{cite web |title=LaShawn Ford to Remain on Mayoral Ballot After Petition Challenge |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/chicago-mayor-lashawn-ford-remains-on-ballot/5178/ |publisher=NBC Chicago |access-date=28 December 2019 |date=12 January 2019}}</ref>

In the polls he was included in, Ford never placed higher than 2%, and most frequently received around 1% support.<ref name=tulchindec19>{{cite web|url=https://static.politico.com/59/80/0e929eb24d7086a6f9209f16d61c/tulchin-polling.jpg.pdf |title=Polling |website=static.politico.com }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Key Takeaways from New Survey ==2026 U.S. House campaign==
On May 21, 2025, Ford filed paperwork with the [[Federal Election Commission]] to run for [[Illinois's 7th congressional district]], currently represented by [[Danny Davis (Illinois politician)|Danny Davis]], in 2026.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dwyer|first=Bill|url=https://www.forestparkreview.com/2025/06/17/danny-davis-to-those-waiting-to-replace-him-people-get-ready/|title=Danny Davis to those waiting to replace him: 'People get ready'|work=[[Forest Park Review]]|date=June 17, 2025|accessdate=July 31, 2025}}</ref> On July 31, Davis announced his retirement and endorsed Ford as his successor.<ref name="Congress"/>

==Personal life==
Ford has a daughter.<ref name=lfcrusader/> He is [[Catholic Church|Catholic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spirituality, young people, marriage discussed at black Catholic gathering - Chicagoland - Chicago Catholic - AoC Portal |url=https://www.chicagocatholic.com/chicagoland/-/article/2016/10/02/spirituality-young-people-marriage-discussed-at-black-catholic-gatheri-2 |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=Chicago Catholic |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Vote Smart {{!}} Facts For All |url=https://justfacts.votesmart.org/candidate/biography/18379/la-shawn-ford |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125032616/https://justfacts.votesmart.org/candidate/biography/18379/la-shawn-ford |archive-date=2025-01-25 |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=Vote Smart |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Legal issues===
On November 29, 2012, Ford was indicted on charges of bank fraud, alleging he provided misleading evidence to obtain a $500,000 extension on a line of credit. The charges state he used the money for personal expenses rather than rehabilitating an owned property, as stated in the loan documentation.<ref name="Indictment">{{cite web|last=Staff|title=Rep. LaShawn Ford indicted on bank fraud charges|date=29 November 2012 |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/news/local/breaking/chi-lashawn-ford-indicted-20121129,0,6480128.story|publisher=Chicago Tribune|access-date=29 November 2012}}</ref> On August 4, 2014, all 17 felony counts of bank fraud and false information against Ford were dropped by federal prosecutors in exchange for his pleading guilty to a single misdemeanor income tax charge, and Ford's trial was removed from the federal docket.<ref>{{cite web|last=Janssen|first=Kim|title=State Rep. La Shawn Ford pleads guilty to misdemeanor|url=http://politics.suntimes.com/article/chicago/state-rep-la-shawn-ford-pleads-guilty-misdemeanor/mon-08042014-755pm|publisher=Chicago Sun Times|access-date=5 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140806054728/http://politics.suntimes.com/article/chicago/state-rep-la-shawn-ford-pleads-guilty-misdemeanor/mon-08042014-755pm|archive-date=6 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Meisner|first=Jason|title=Surprising plea deal in state Rep. Ford's bank fraud case|date=4 August 2014 |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/news/local/breaking/chi-state-rep-ford-to-plead-guilty-to-bank-fraud-20140804-story.html|publisher=Chicago Tribune|access-date=5 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Marin|first=Carol|title=Feds back off on ruining a good man's life|url=http://www.suntimes.com/news/marin/29057910-452/feds-back-off-ruining-a-good-mans-life.html|publisher=Chicago Sun Times|access-date=5 August 2014}}</ref>
